name: Murata-grm_GRM1885C1H103JA01
title: GRM1885C1H103JA01: 10000 pF, 50 V DC, C0G multilayer ceramic chip capacitor, 1608M (0603)

source.revision: Reference sheet, specifications as of Jun.17,2026

summary: GRM1885C1H103JA01 is a two-terminal multilayer ceramic chip capacitor in the GRM family, 10000 pF ±5% rated 50 V DC, with a C0G (EIA) dielectric whose temperature coefficient is 0 ±30 ppm/°C. The chip is 1.6 × 0.8 × 0.8 mm (1608M metric, 0603 inch), works from -55 to 125 °C and may be mounted by flow or reflow soldering. The last letter of the part number picks the reel: D, W, J or V.
key_figures: more than 10000 MΩ at rated voltage

operation.text: Intended for consumer equipment, industrial equipment, medical devices of GHTF classes A and B and non-implant class C, and automotive infotainment and comfort equipment. Aircraft, aerospace, undersea, power plant control, medical, transportation, traffic control, disaster prevention, industrial data processing and combustion control uses, and others needing equal reliability, are outside the specified applications.
Body length 1.6 ±0.1 mm, width 0.8 ±0.1 mm, height 0.8 ±0.1 mm. Each end termination wraps 0.2 to 0.5 mm onto the body (e), and the bare gap between the two terminations (g) is 0.5 mm at least.

operation.topic: Rated voltage with AC or pulses
operation.text: The rated voltage is the DC limit for every waveform: with AC on top of DC the zero-to-peak value, and for pure AC or pulses the peak-to-peak value, may not go past 50 V. Surges, ESD and other abnormal voltages are held to the same limit. Overvoltage can break down the dielectric layers and short the part; how quickly depends on voltage and ambient temperature.

With continuous AC or pulse current the dielectric loss heats the chip. For parts rated below 100 V DC the load is kept such that the body rises less than 20 °C above a 25 °C ambient, and the surface temperature including self-heating stays within the 125 °C operating limit.

Store at +5 to +40 °C and 20 to 70% relative humidity, preferably below 30 °C, away from corrosive gases (hydrogen sulfide, sulfur dioxide, chlorine, ammonia), direct sunlight and condensation. After six months from delivery the packaging and mounting are checked; after one year the solderability is checked as well.

High dielectric constant types such as X7R and X5R shift capacitance with temperature, with applied DC and AC voltage, and downward with time (aging), and can hum mechanically in AC or pulse circuits; in time-constant and other tight-tolerance circuits those effects are checked in the actual system. Capacitance is measured at the voltage and frequency of the specification.

Board bending stresses a chip least when its long axis lies across the bending direction. Near a separation line, turning the chip parallel to the line, adding slits and moving the chip away from the line each lower the stress; all three together are best. Chips are kept as far as possible from screw holes.

Capacitors removed from equipment are not reused. Parts from long storage are checked for solderability, and heat-treated before capacitance is measured. Sn-Zn solders reduce reliability and are discussed with Murata first.
The nozzle's lowest point is set so it does not flex the board, with support under the board, and worn locating claws and dirty nozzles are replaced on a schedule because both crack chips.

Both board and parts are preheated so that the difference between solder and component surface stays within ΔT≦190 ℃ for the 18 size. Peak is 240 to 260 ℃ in air or nitrogen. Too low a peak risks poor wetting, voids, whiskers, weak joints, poor self-alignment and tombstoning. Too much paste raises the fillet and the cracking risk; too little leaves a weak joint.

Flow soldering is allowed for GRM 155, 18, 21 and 31 sizes with ΔT≦150 ℃, preheat peak 100 to 120 ℃ and solder peak 250 to 260 ℃. Long or hot soldering leaches the terminations and can lose capacitance. The fillet top stays below the chip thickness. A chip glued before flow soldering needs an adhesive that keeps its strength through moisture and heat, is non-corrosive, insulating, halogen-free and non-toxic.

Iron rework of the 18 size uses a tip of 350 ℃ max. with the board preheated to 150 ℃ min., a tip of ø3 mm or smaller kept off the chip body, and solder wire of ø0.5 mm or smaller, working quickly and letting the board cool slowly. A spot heater is held 5 mm or more away at 45°, at 400 °C max. for less than 10 s.

Ultrasonic cleaning can resonate the board and crack chips, so the process is proven first. In-circuit test probes need support pins under the board close to the probe. Coating resins should have low cure shrinkage, a thermal expansion close to the chip's, low moisture absorption and no strong acids; silicone can serve as a stress-buffering undercoat and epoxy as a low-moisture resin.
Flux halide content is 0.1% max., applied thinly; strong acid fluxes are avoided. Termination leaching may not exceed 25% of the chip end edge length, or 25% of the termination length when mounted.

A router separator is preferred; a jig or disc separator is acceptable only with controlled handling, V-groove design and blade alignment, and hand or nipper separation is not used. Boards are held at the edges with both hands, supported when leaded parts, sockets or connectors are inserted, and screwed down with a torque driver without forcing a warped board flat. Dropped boards and dropped capacitors are not used.

General MLCC products target a device life of about 10 years, extending past 10 years at no more than 80% of rated voltage and at least 20 °C below the maximum operating temperature. Consumer-specific products target more than 5 years under the same derating. The useful life is the time to 1% cumulative failure in continuous use; the curves are estimates, not guarantees.

Water, brine, condensation and corrosive or volatile gases and solvents can short the part or corrode its terminations. A capacitor cracked by dropping or board flex can lose insulation resistance and short, so a circuit where a short could cause shock, smoke or fire needs a fail-safe such as a fuse. The series is not safety-standard certified. Disposal is by a licensed industrial waste contractor.
